Issued at 314 PM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Troughing hanging near/off either coast of the CONUS today...with 
somewhat more progressive flow across Canada, with a handful of PV 
niblets over Saskatchewan and Manitoba as of 12z helping to flatten 
ridge axis a bit over central North America; 534dam upper trough 
over Quebec. Yesterday's shortwave trough diving southeastward 
across the Lower Great Lakes this morning, headed for opening upper 
wave off New England; upstream, 80kt southerly upper jet and 
excellent difluence with abundant moisture transport into the 
southwestern US. Southwesterly flow in the low levels sneaks up into 
the northern Plains as well...with warm advection up into Manitoba 
ahead of the next northern stream trough. Coldest air attm not 
surprisingly well to our northeast beneath that upper low, with 
850mb temps -8C and colder; here in Northern Michigan, we remain in 
the 6C+ range. Quite a bit of low-level moisture oozing southward 
behind what is left of the front from last night as high pressure 
builds to our north; not surprisingly seeing quite a bit of dense 
fog and low stratus this morning, esp north of M-32...and this has 
been a bit slow to mix out, esp near the coast. Appears most model 
guidance is trying to dry things out too quickly across the area 
this morning...as dewpoints generally hang around 43-50F as of 
14z...and low clouds struggle to mix out (KPLN holding firmly to 
200ft cloud bases, even approaching peak heating).  

High pressure will continue to hang out near/overtop of Michigan 
tonight into Friday...resulting in another round of patchy fog 
tonight. Return flow strengthens upstream Friday into Saturday...as 
upstream troughing slowly attempts to transit eastward...though 
northern and southern streams appear to remain split, with the upper 
low getting left behind in the southwestern US as a more potent 
upper low (and attendant surface system) tracks ENE-ward across 
central Canada into Hudson Bay by Sunday. This should punch down 
ridging into the area, and will have potential to drape a boundary 
across the Midwest/Eastern US going into the start of the work week. 
The SW US energy finally rides up along this BCZ as it ejects 
eastward toward midweek, fading out as additional upstream energy 
moves into the PacNW, potentially quite hot-on-its-heels...though 
there is some uncertainty in the timing/evolution of this latter 
feature for midweek and beyond. In fact, there remains quite a bit 
of uncertainty in the forecast for the latter half of next week, 
pending the evolution of said feature and whether or not it digs 
deeper into the Midwest or not...though it could at the very least 
trend somewhat cooler/more seasonable for early next week.

FORECAST DETAILS...

Fog again tonight...think the song will remain much the same tonight 
as last night, thanks to high pressure still hanging out in the 
region (nearly overhead tonight, in fact). The low stratus/fog deck 
is finally beginning to erode across the EUP and northern Lakes 
Michigan and Huron as of 18z...but still trying to hang on across NE 
Lower MI where there is some semblance of upsloping on N/NE flow. 
Not expecting much change to the air mass going forward, noting 
little in the way of advection except for some subtle cooling at 
925mb...though there are some signals for slightly higher theta-e 
air over central Lake Superior/N. WI to drift southeastward towards 
us with time. Conceptually, think that the best chance of fog 
tonight will be across the EUP into parts of northern Lower where 
skies have cleared a bit quicker today and should allow for more 
efficient radiational cooling after sundown. The sticky wicket will 
be NE Lower and that slow-to-dissipate stratus deck; if we don't mix 
it out during the heating of the day today, it's liable to stick 
around tonight and keep a blanket over the area. It may again take a 
hot minute to mix out Friday morning, similar to today, though it 
should rotate out of the area with time as return flow kicks up over 
WI. Think we could fog again Friday night as well, though think the 
best shot at this would be toward our Saginaw Bay region.  

Rain chances possible Sunday...Next chance of rain likely holds off 
till Sunday as that front drapes in, the tail end of a much stronger 
storm passing by well to our north. Overall idea suggests the 
boundary will drape in and stall over southern MI for the start of 
the work week...and do think there could be a decent little feed of 
moisture into our area ahead of the front Saturday night into Sunday 
that could be enough to overcome the otherwise dry low/mid-level 
conditions we've been dealing with for the last few days or more, 
and there could be enough forcing to squeeze a little bit out of the 
atmosphere. However, would not be surprised if we ended up quiet/dry 
overall. Best chance for measurable rainfall would be the EUP closer 
to better forcing along the front.
